heading: INT. AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER, SMALL REGIONAL AIRPORT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER, SMALL REGIONAL AIRPORT - NIGHT
A glass-walled octagon above a dark runway.
Radar scope glows green.
A cold cup of coffee sits beside a ham sandwich with one bite out of it.
OSWALD "OZZIE" FAIRWEATHER (60s, headset, cardigan) sits at the console, steady and unhurried.
Next to him stands his granddaughter, PRUDENCE "PRU" FAIRWEATHER (17, school uniform, backpack), holding a notebook.
She is supposed to be doing homework.
She is not.
Two others fill the cramped room.
One is MARTIN ESPERANZA (30s, shift supervisor, tie loosened), who hovers over the radar.
The other is a trainee, JUNE TAKAHASHI (19, apron over uniform, nervous), who clutches a clipboard.
Pru, if you're going to watch, watch properly. Come around here.
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: Grandpa, I'm fine.
units.name: PRU

units.text: Come on.
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: She steps beside him.
He nods to the scope.
That blip is a Cessna. November-Four-Two-Seven. See how she drifts?
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: Why?
units.name: PRU

units.text: Crosswind. He's fighting it.
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: Pru leans closer.
Her breath fogs the glass.
Tower, Cessna Four-Two-Seven, ten miles out, requesting landing.
units.name: PILOT

units.text: Ozzie squeezes the mic.
Four-Two-Seven, Tower, runway two-seven, wind two-six-zero at eighteen gusting twenty-five. Say your fuel state.
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: Tower, Four-Two-Seven, thirty minutes of fuel. We're good.
units.name: PILOT

units.text: Thirty minutes. In that wind.
units.name: MARTIN

units.text: Should I call the fire crew?
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: MARTIN

units.text: Ozzie hands the headset to Pru.
Grandpa, no.
units.name: PRU

units.text: Just say what I say. "Four-Two-Seven, cleared to land."
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: She hesitates, then pulls the headset on.
Her voice shakes.
Four-Two-Seven, cleared to land.
units.name: PRU

units.text: Cleared to land, Four-Two-Seven. Who's this? You sound young.
units.name: PILOT

units.text: Um. I'm... training.
units.name: PRU

units.text: Good job, trainee. See you on the ground.
units.name: PILOT

units.text: Pru stares at her grandfather, wide-eyed.
He chuckles and pats her shoulder.
Eyes on the scope, Pru. That's the whole job.
units.name: OZZIE

units.text: Below them, tiny landing lights wobble through the dark, steadying, lowering.
They all watch it touch down.
